summary: The fleet can now be asked one question at a time instead of one appliance at a time. A new federated search on the control plane asks every node an operator can reach — in parallel, over the existing mTLS control channel — what it saw, and merges the answers newest-first into a single list: object classes the AI detected, and the plates and people it recognized, narrowed by node, site, object, plate or person text, time window and confidence. Recognized identities do not live in the object index, so each node answers from both: presence intervals from its metadata recorder, and the license-plate and face identities recorded on its alerts. Results carry the node, the site and the CAMERA'S OWN NAME, because every recorder numbers its cameras from one and "camera 3" means a different place on each. Objects are searched under the node's Objects grant and identities under its AI-log grant, so no role can reach through the fleet for data it could not read on the appliance itself, and every estate-wide search is written to the audit trail with the terms it used. The Objects screen now shows a coverage line above the results on every search — which nodes answered, which did not and why, and how far back the answer is actually complete. That line is the feature: the browser used to fan out to each node itself and silently swallow the ones that failed, so a recorder that had been unreachable for a week simply contributed no rows, and an investigator reading an empty table could not tell "the fleet never saw it" from "the half of the fleet that would have seen it was never asked".
compatibility: Purely additive: two new read-only endpoints on each node (GET /api/observations/search, GET /api/vision/alerts/identities) and two on the control plane (GET /api/nodes/search, GET /api/nodes/search/labels). No new tables, no migration, no configuration. The control-plane routes sit under /api/nodes on purpose, so every role already granted GET there keeps the fleet search it has today without an administrator having to notice and grant a new path. A MIXED-VERSION FLEET IS EXPECTED AND HANDLED: a node still on an older build has no search endpoint and is reported as 'needs upgrade' in the coverage block rather than quietly contributing nothing — the whole point being that a node which was not searched is never counted as a node that saw nothing. A search is bounded per node (default 200 rows, 15s) and in total, and any node that hit its bound reports how far back its answer reaches, so the result says where completeness ends rather than presenting a prefix as the whole truth. Unlike the node's own Objects grid, the fleet search returns sightings with no playable footage — a detect-only camera at a remote gate is often the only thing that saw the vehicle — and labels them 'no footage' rather than promising a clip that is never coming. There is deliberately no paging offset: an offset cannot be honoured across independent sources without silently dropping rows, so a wide search is narrowed by its time window instead. Live-benched against a real two-node fleet with genuinely adopted nodes on the real fleet CA and control channel, 36/36, including stopping a node mid-investigation and confirming the search reports it by name with a reason, keeps returning the reachable node's sightings, and refuses to call itself complete. A browser check of the rewritten screen caught a real defect on the way: sightings from cameras that record nothing were labelled 'Recording…' forever, promising footage that could never arrive.
